comments.body: Related, from building the stall notice's reasons (2026-10-16): when a wake is held behind something only a person can answer - a covered prompt such as Claude Code's feedback-draft box, or a blocked agent - the stall notice names it after two minutes but tells only the group's poster. Raising that notice to the person as well is a narrower first step toward this card's escalation.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A pane sat blocked at a permission dialog for over six hours overnight, and the only notice went to an agent that could not answer it.

2026-10-12/13, laptop, from tooling feedback (Muster version not stated, 0.15.0 by the notice): an overnight orchestrator (Claude Code, bypass mode) stopped at a background subagent's permission dialog from 23:43 to 06:25, so nothing ran for about 6h40m. The only targeted notice was 0.15.0's `@muster` stall message, sent to the poster of the unread message, itself an idle agent.

`crates/muster-daemon/src/messages/stalls.rs` tells only the poster, once per stall, and only when a message is unread. The `[notifications] blocked` banner fires once and is easy to miss on a machine nobody is watching.

Expected: a pane blocked longer than some threshold escalates once to someone who can answer: `@human`, or a watcher pane named in config. A per-pane opt-in for "runs unattended" would keep interactive use quiet. The threshold, the target and the opt-in are design calls for whoever picks this up; record them in the commit or in `docs/configuration.md`.
title: A pane blocked at a dialog for hours tells only an agent that cannot answer
